notes: Absolute loss evaluates means; the posterior median is its Bayes rule.
Max risk describes a finite signal grid at fixed nuisances, not a minimax theorem.
Gamma plug-in ignores nuisance uncertainty and the zero atom; its prior is diffuse.
Laplace plugs in nuisances and retains the atom and boundary slope. It uses a linear tangent for nonpositive local precision and can fail badly.
The learned neural distribution approximates the posterior; SBC can reject it.
HPD output ranks zero-volume atoms first, then continuous cell densities. Summaries describe its inclusive hull, while the raw accepted mask can be disconnected.
SBC checks prior-averaged calibration and does not establish fixed-theta coverage.
Zero SBC p-values represent floating-point underflow; figures show p<1e-300.
Risk comparisons use common observations across estimators and analysis priors.
Gaussian efficiency quadrature does not impose a physical efficiency bound.
All four SBC samplers use one seed, so they are scored on the same 1000 prior draws (common random numbers); their p-values are not independent tests.

Paired fields use the SE of per-draw differences on shared draws or toys. excess_squared_risk is E[(d - d_ref)^2]; it equals the excess squared Bayes risk because the reference, the reality-prior grid posterior mean, is the Bayes rule up to quadrature error.

posterior_content is the mass that the reporting posterior puts inside its own equal-tailed interval. When the zero atom holds at least alpha/2, the interval starts at 0 and holds at least 1 - alpha/2.
max_grid_risk_common_slice uses only the b=3 rows, which every method has; max_grid_risk uses each method's own slices.
neural_vs_exact_posterior bins the grid posterior into the network's classes and reports KL(exact || neural) on the Bayes-risk draws.
